items.title: Nicki Parrott interviewed by Monk Rowe. Utica, New York, November 6, 2010 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: Son. And his mother, who passed away recently in Philadelphia.

ctx.x: is a wonderful piano player. I think it paid like 30 bucks or something like that. It was like a lunchtime gig at the Film Center. So I did Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday I worked in fashion selling prints to fashion designers. And that world was crazy. That was a crazy world. The whole fashion world. Skinny girls and gay guys pretty much. So I thought well, this is something different. You know, very competitive and but interesting kind of, it was creative. And so I did that for eight months. And I sold all these…

Son. And his mother, who passed away recently in Philadelphia. A wonderful piano player. But they kind of took me in and it was just really a beautiful experience. I think I did that for like a year even, just playing there a couple of times a week, and it was just like a way to get your feet wet. It was a fun gig you know, it was just for people having coffee before they went to the movie. I didn’t care you know what I mean? You just want to play and get out there. And then at night if I could afford it I’d go…
